summary: During the mounted floor-gold theft branch, the JS replay stops when steal.js:stealgold calls y_monnam for the hero’s steed, because the module uses y_monnam without importing it. C steal.c:stealgold makes the same naming call after transferring floor gold to the leprechaun. The saved C/JS prefix matches through 384 prior steps; the thrown ReferenceError at step 385 prevents all later output.

source.branch: A leprechaun attacks a mounted hero while a gold pile lies under the steed and the hero carries no gold or carries a smaller pile. C transfers the floor stack and names the steed in its message; JS reaches the same branch but its y_monnam binding is missing.
callers: uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_sgld() calls steal.c:stealgold() when a monster attacks the hero with AD_SGLD and is not cancelled.
js/uhitm.js:mhitm_ad_sgld() calls js/steal.js:stealgold() in the corresponding monster-to-hero attack branch.
dependencies: steal.c:stealgold() calls do_name.c:y_monnam() for a mounted hero; js/steal.js already imports related naming functions from js/do_name.js but omits y_monnam.

evidence: C source steal.c:58-116 transfers floor gold first, then uses y_monnam(u.usteed) to build the possessive in the mounted message; no RNG or separate naming branch precedes that call.
JavaScript js/steal.js:1242-1271 follows the same floorGold branch and calls y_monnam(who,state,env), while its do_name.js import list includes Adjmonnam, Monnam and Some_Monnam but omits y_monnam.

The admitted v73 case is designed with a mounted hero, no carried gold, a floor gold pile and an adjacent leprechaun. The retained C/JS comparison matches 385 screens and 2319 RNG calls before the step-385 ReferenceError; the case queue records the resulting stop error and zero complete session outputs.
